The MemOffset (operand 2) is the VALUE-bearing operand the matcher keys on; its single imm12.hilo24 wire (word0) carries the displacement, split lo→word0 / hi→word1 by the encoder. MemBase (operand 1, scale==1) carries no bits (membase.noscale, word0). `immMin:4096`/`immMax:16777215`; a >16MiB offset stays fail-loud (D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-16MIB). width:64 (a frame address is Ptr-width); the disjoint imm-range makes it unambiguous against the single-word variant above regardless of width.

FRAME-RELATIVE lea (MOVZ/MOVK + EXTENDED-register 3-word form, D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-16MIB) — `lea Xd, [sp + #disp]` with disp in (0xFFFFFF, 0x7FFFFFFF] (>16 MiB, ≤2 GiB). The GEP's high-element address (e.g. `int big[5000000]; big[4999999]` at sp+~20MB) under a >16MiB frame. Emits THREE words, SCRATCH-FREE: the displacement materializes into the lea's DEST reg Xd, then an extended-register ADD off sp. word0 = `MOVZ Xd, #(disp & 0xFFFF)` (0xD2800000, Rd=Xd via resultSlot), word1 = `MOVK Xd, #((disp>>16) & 0xFFFF), LSL #16` (0xF2A00000, Rd=Xd via extraResultSlots word1.rd), word2 = `ADD Xd, sp, Xd` (the EXTENDED-register form 0x8B2063E0: option=011 UXTX, bit 21 set, Rn=sp=31 baked, Rd=Xd + Rm=Xd via extraResultSlots word2.rd/word2.rm). The dest reg threads through ALL THREE words (resultSlot=rd word0 + three extraResultSlots) — no separate scratch needed. The MemOffset (operand 2) is the VALUE-bearing operand the matcher keys on; its single imm32.movzmovk wire (word0) carries the displacement, split lo16→word0 / hi16→word1 by the encoder. Operand 0 (base=sp) → word2's `rn` (re-confirming the baked sp=31); operand 1 (membase, scale==1) → membase.noscale (word2, no bits). `immMin:16777216`/`immMax:2147483647`; a >2GiB offset goes negative through int32 → fail-loud (D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-2GIB).

NEGATIVE-DISP lea (single word, D-AS4-ARM64-NEGATIVE-DISP-LEA-NATIVE-SUB) — `lea Xd, [base + #disp]` with disp in [-4095, -1] = AArch64 `SUB Xd, Xn, #|disp|`. The `p[-1]`/`z[-1]` char-buffer lookback (a NEGATIVE const-disp GEP) that x86 encodes in one signed-disp32 `lea` but arm64's UNSIGNED imm12 ADD form could not — c94 gives it a NATIVE single-instruction SUB (replacing c93's materialize-into-a-fresh-GPR + base+index fold, which cost 5-7 instructions incl. a dead const). The negative MIRROR of the positive `ADD Xd,Xn,#imm12` variant above, op-bit SET: single fixed word 0xD1000000 (3506438144 = the ADD-imm base 0x91000000 | 0x40000000, sf=1 op=1 sub S=0 sh=0), shared with `sub`'s imm12 variant. base_reg→Rn (5..9), result→Rd (0..4), MemOffset→Imm12 (bits 10..21 — the encoder writes |disp| there; the SUB base makes it a subtract). MemBase carries no bits (scale must be 1, membase.noscale). `negValue:true` routes ONLY a NEGATIVE memoffset here (the sign matcher); `immMax:4095` bounds |disp|≤4095 (a larger magnitude falls through to the shifted / MOVZ-MOVK negative variants below). SUB imm encoding verified vs ARM ARM C6.2.* (add/subtract immediate: sf|op|S|100010|sh|imm12|Rn|Rd) + aarch64-gcc objdump.

NEGATIVE-DISP lea (shifted imm12 word-pair, D-AS4-ARM64-NEGATIVE-DISP-LEA-NATIVE-SUB) — `lea Xd, [base + #disp]` with |disp| in (4095, 0xFFFFFF]. The negative mirror of the positive shifted-imm12 ADD word-pair, op-bit SET: word0 = `SUB Xd, Xn, #(|disp| & 0xFFF)` (0xD1000000, sh=0), word1 = `SUB Xd, Xd, #((|disp|>>12) & 0xFFF), LSL #12` (0xD1400000 = 0xD1000000|0x400000, sh=1). SCRATCH-FREE: word1 reads its OWN dest (Xd) — extraResultSlots thread the result reg into word1.Rd AND word1.Rn. The MemOffset (operand 2) is the sign-matched value operand; its single imm12.hilo24 wire (word0) carries |disp|, split lo→word0 / hi→word1 by the encoder. `negValue:true` + `immMin:4096`/`immMax:16777215` (|disp| magnitude); a >16MiB magnitude falls through to the MOVZ/MOVK form below. Fixed words = the `sub` opcode's shifted word-pair.

NEGATIVE-DISP lea (MOVZ/MOVK + EXTENDED-register 3-word form, D-AS4-ARM64-NEGATIVE-DISP-LEA-NATIVE-SUB) — `lea Xd, [base + #disp]` with |disp| in (0xFFFFFF, 0x7FFFFFFF]. The negative mirror of the positive MOVZ/MOVK 3-word form, op-bit SET on the operation word. SCRATCH-FREE: |disp| materializes into the lea's DEST reg Xd, then an EXTENDED-register SUB off the base. word0 = `MOVZ Xd, #(|disp| & 0xFFFF)` (0xD2800000, Rd=Xd via resultSlot), word1 = `MOVK Xd, #((|disp|>>16) & 0xFFFF), LSL #16` (0xF2A00000, Rd=Xd via extraResultSlots word1.rd), word2 = `SUB Xd, Xn, Xd` (the EXTENDED-register form 0xCB206000: sf=1 op=1 sub, option=011 UXTX bits 15:13, bit 21 set, Rn=base wired 5..9, Rd=Xd + Rm=Xd via extraResultSlots word2.rd/word2.rm). Unlike the POSITIVE 3-word form (which bakes Rn=sp=31), the NEGATIVE form WIRES Rn to the base register (operand 0, word2) — a derived-pointer `p[-N]` base, not sp. The dest reg threads through all three words. MemOffset (operand 2) sign-matched; its imm32.movzmovk wire (word0) carries |disp|, split lo16→word0 / hi16→word1. `negValue:true` + `immMin:16777216`/`immMax:2147483647`; a magnitude > 2 GiB flows through int32 as a value whose |x| is unrepresentable → no variant → fail-loud (the residual, mirrors the positive >2GiB gap). SUB-extended base 0xCB206000 = the positive lea word2 0x8B2063E0 minus the baked Rn=sp (0x3E0) with the ADD op-bit flipped to SUB (0x8B→0xCB), verified by bit-decode.

BASE+INDEX lea (D-AS4-ARM64-BASE-INDEX-LEA) — `lea Xd, [base + index*1 + 0]` = AArch64 `ADD Xd, Xn, Xm` (shifted-register add, LSL #0). The 4-op form `lowerGep` emits for an indexed pointer access `p[n]` ([base_reg, index_reg, MemBase(scale=1), MemOffset(disp=0)]), MIRRORING x86_64's 4-op SIB lea so the GEP stays target-blind (closing the gap that made `p[n]` fail loud on arm64 for int AND char alike). The GEP emits scale=1 + disp=0 ALWAYS today, so this single ADD is the complete realization: base→Rn (5..9), index→Rm (16..20), result→Rd (0..4); MemBase→membase.noscale (scale MUST be 1, fail-loud) and MemOffset→memoffset.zero (disp MUST be 0 — the register-add form has NO displacement field, and bits 10..21 overlap Rm so an Imm12 wiring would corrupt it; fail-loud on nonzero). Fixed word 0x8B000000 (the ADD reg-reg base, shared with `add`'s reg-reg variant). A scale!=1 (typed-array Gep scaling by sizeof(T)) needs the shifted form `ADD Xd,Xn,Xm,LSL #log2(scale)` — a FUTURE consumer (D-AS4-ARM64-INDEXED-LEA-SCALE, co-design with ML6 address-mode synthesis), NOT built speculatively.

TLS C2 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): 2-op thread-pointer-offset form — `lea Xd, [tp + tpoff(sym)]` = the AArch64 local-exec ADD/ADD hi12/lo12 word-pair (gcc -ftls-model=local-exec parity): word0 = `ADD Xd, Xn(tp), #hi12, LSL #12` (0x91400000 = ADD-imm sh=1, imm12 field ZERO — reloc tls-tprel-hi12 patches (S+A)>>12 in, range-checked [0, 0xFFFFFF]), word1 = `ADD Xd, Xd, #lo12` (0x91000000 = ADD-imm sh=0, imm12 ZERO — reloc tls-tprel-lo12 patches (S+A)&0xFFF in, magnitude-free). S = the POSITIVE Variant-I tpoff the walker bit-cast into symbolVa (addTlsSymbolOffsets). SCRATCH-FREE via the SAME extraResultSlots threading the ADRP+ADD [symbol] variant above uses: word1 reads its own dest (Xd → word1.Rd AND word1.Rn). Operand 0 (the `tlsbase`-produced tp reg) → word0.Rn; operand 1 (the SymbolRef) emits BOTH relocations through the generic sym.patch marker — at word offsets 0 and 4 of the macro, both against the same symbol. Distinct guard [reg, symbol] — no other lea variant carries that shape. The x86 twin is the [reg, symbol] memreloc.disp32 lea in x86_64.target.json; the LIR the lowering emits is IDENTICAL (tlsbase reg + lea [reg, sym]) — only the declared encodings differ.

opcodes.$comment: D-LK-ARM64-EXTERN-DATA-ADDR-PIE-GOT (TF-C52): GOT-address materialization macro -- `adrp Xd,:got:sym` + `ldr Xd,[Xd,:got_lo12:sym]`. Loads the RUN-TIME address of an undefined/preemptible extern (function OR data) OUT of a GOT slot the FINAL (foreign) linker synthesizes, so a foreign default-PIE link of the emitted relocatable `.o`/`.a` accepts it (an absolute ADRP+ADD page-pair against a symbol that may bind externally is rejected 'when making a shared object'). A DISTINCT MnemonicSlot (the `tlsbase` precedent), NOT a new `lea` variant -- a `lea` `[symbol]` variant would COLLIDE with the existing absolute ADRP+ADD `[symbol]` lea (ambiguous encoder match); MIR->LIR `lowerGlobalAddr`'s value-form arm emits THIS mnemonic explicitly (keyed on the capability-derived `externAddrGotSymbols_` set) for an `&extern` VALUE. word0 = ADRP Xd, sym@GOTPAGE (0x90000000=2415919104): Rd at bits 0..4 via resultSlot; immlo[30:29]+immhi[23:5] left ZERO -- the adr_got_page reloc (R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE) patches the GOT-page delta. word1 = LDR Xd, [Xd, #:got_lo12:sym] (0xF9400000=4181721088, the 64-bit unsigned-offset LDR base shared with `load_u`'s width-64 word): Rt at 0..4 AND Rn at 5..9 (BOTH = the result reg via extraResultSlots -- the LDR reads the ADRP page-base register into itself); imm12[21:10] left ZERO -- the ld64_got_lo12 reloc (R_AARCH64_LD64_GOT_LO12_NC) patches the scaled slot offset. BYTE-STRUCTURE-IDENTICAL to the ADRP+ADD `lea` `[symbol]` variant (same resultSlot/extraResultSlots threading) except the 2nd word is an LDR (a load, not an add) and the two sym.patch wires carry the GOT relocs. DSS never APPLIES these relocs (the exec_reloc_apply kernel arm fail-loud-refuses); the foreign linker resolves the GOT slot.

D-AS3-BLOCK-REL-IMM19/26 (ARM64 conditional control-flow): integer compare writing the NZCV flags, no GPR result. AArch64 `CMP Xn, Xm` is an alias for `SUBS XZR, Xn, Xm` (subtract-and-set-flags discarding the result into the zero register). Fixed word 0xEB00001F = SUBS (sf=1, op=1, S=1) with Rd=31 (XZR) baked in; Rn at bits 5..9, Rm at bits 16..20. Mirrors x86's `cmp` LIR shape (InvalidLirReg result, 2 reg operands) — ML5 lowerICmp + lowerCondBr emit it before the conditional branch. NO resultSlot (the flags are the implicit output). Reuses the Rn/Rm slots already exercised by the add/sub reg-reg variants.

variants.$comment: FC3 c2: CMP Wn, Wm = SUBS WZR, Wn, Wm — 0x6B00001F (the X-form 0xEB00001F with sf=0). A U32 compare MUST read 32 bits — a bitcast-from-negative operand carries sign-extended upper bits the X-form would misread.

FC3.5 sweep-c1: CMP Xn, #imm12 = SUBS XZR, Xn, #imm12 — add/subtract (immediate), ARM ARM C6.2.395: sf=1 [31] | op=1 sub [30] | S=1 [29] | 100010 [28:23] | sh=0 [22] | imm12 [21:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd=XZR=31 [4:0] = 0xF100001F. FIRST consumer: the MIR->LIR non-fused CondBr arm's `cmp cond, #0` over a PHI-produced Bool (a short-circuit `&&`/`||` result used as an if/while condition cannot fuse with its compare). x86's cmp had its reg-imm form from the start; this arm64 gap was masked until the S2 marker fix let logical-op conditions reach codegen. Reuses the Imm12 slot (bits 10..21) the callconv's sub-sp frame adjust already exercises; the walker range-checks 0..4095 fail-loud.
FC3.5 sweep-c1: CMP Wn, #imm12 — the X-form with sf=0: 0x7100001F. The 32-bit sibling per the FC3-c2 width axis (a U32-typed Bool-ish compare reads 32 bits).

opcodes.$comment: D-AS3-BLOCK-REL-IMM19/26: unconditional intra-function jump. AArch64 `B <label>` (encoding 0x14000000, opcode bits 26..31 = 0b000101). The 26-bit imm field (bits 0..25, SCALED by 4) is the SIGNED word displacement to the target block — resolved at ASSEMBLE time via the Imm26 slot + per-function patch list (NOT a linker relocation; the same Imm26 slot is symbol-bearing for the BL/`call` form, but a BlockRef operand here selects the intra-function path). Operand[0] is a BlockRef naming the target basic block. Mirrors x86's `jmp` (E9 rel32). Imm26's ±128 MiB reach covers any single function.

D-CSUBSET-COMPUTED-GOTO: indirect branch `BR Xn` — 0xD61F0000 | Rn<<5 (unconditional branch to a register, NO link/return-address — the BLR sibling captures one). fixedWord 3592355840 = 0xD61F0000; mirrors the BLR row (0xD63F0000, same D6 family — BR clears bit 21). Rn at bits 5..9 via the `rn` slot. The MIR IndirectBr lowers to this; the target-address register is materialized by a preceding adrp+add `lea` of the target block's synthetic symbol (BlockAddress). terminatorKind indirect-br → variadic address-taken successors.

D-AS3-BLOCK-REL-IMM19/26: conditional intra-function jump with mandatory fallthrough. 2-WORD macro: `B.cond <ifTrue>` (word 0) then `B <ifFalse>` (word 1) — the AArch64 analog of x86's `0F 8x rel32; E9 rel32` compound. word0 = B.cond base 0x54000000 (opcode bits 24..31 = 0b01010100, bit 4 = 0); the cond nibble (bits 0..3) comes from the inst's payload (TargetCondCode) via `condCodeFromPayload` + the schema's `condCodeEncoding` table; the 19-bit signed PC-relative offset (bits 5..23, scaled by 4) goes to the Imm19 slot → ifTrue block. word1 = B base 0x14000000 with the Imm26 slot → ifFalse (fallthrough) block. Both displacements resolve at assemble time (BlockRef operands, no relocation). operand[0]=ifTrue (taken when cond holds), operand[1]=ifFalse. A future optimizer elides word1 when ifFalse is the next-laid-out block (D-OPT-JCC-FALLTHROUGH). Mirrors the x86 jcc wiring + the lea multi-word fixedWords+wordIndex shape.

opcodes.$comment: c78 (D-CSUBSET-FLOAT-NEG-ENCODING): FNEG Dd, Dn — scalar double floating-point NEGATE, FP data-processing (1 source). arm64 has a NATIVE fp-negate (unlike x86, which has no fneg instruction and takes the sign-mask XORPD fallback in mir_to_lir — the two realizations diverge by CAPABILITY, probed via this opcode's declared-encoding presence). IEEE-exact by construction: FNEG flips ONLY the sign bit (bit 63), so -(+0.0)=-0.0, -(-0.0)=+0.0, and -NaN preserves the payload while flipping the sign — the signed-zero + NaN-sign semantics C requires. Base 0x1E614000 = 000 11110 [31:24] | ftype=01 double [23:22] | 1 [21] | opcode=000010 FNEG [20:15] | 10000 [14:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0] (ARM ARM C7.2 FNEG scalar; opcode 000001 would be FABS, 000000 FMOV). 1-source NATIVE — Rd (result), Rn (wire 0 = the value negated). NO requires2Address (Rd and Rn are independent, like neg/not). F32 sibling FNEG Sd, Sn = ftype=00 -> base 0x1E214000 rides the width axis (D-form keyed 64, S-form keyed 32).

variants.$comment: FNEG Sd, Sn — ftype=00 single, base 0x1E214000 = 505495552.

opcodes.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c2 (FCmp LIR lowering): FCMP Dn, Dm — floating-point compare writing NZCV, no register result (the float sibling of `cmp`). Base 0x1E602000 = 000 11110 [31:24] | ftype=01 [23:22] | 1 [21] | Rm [20:16] | op=00 [15:14] | 1000 [13:10] | Rn [9:5] | opcode2=00000 [4:0] (ARM ARM C7.2 FCMP; opcode2 bit4=1 would be FCMPE, the signaling form — DSS does not model the FP environment, so the quiet FCMP serves all predicates; the NZCV comparison RESULTS are identical). F32 sibling FCMP Sn, Sm = 0x1E202000 (ftype=00). NZCV outcomes: equal → Z=1(C=1); less → N=1; greater → C=1; unordered → C=1,V=1 — the truth table the float condCodeEncoding arms below realize (full derivation at mir_to_lir floatCmpPlan).

variants.$comment: FC3.5: FCMP Sn, Sm — ftype=00 single, base 0x1E202000.

opcodes.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c2: float↔float precision change for MIR FPTrunc/FPExt — FCVT (scalar): 000 11110 [31:24] | type [23:22] = SOURCE type | 1 [21] | 0001 [20:17] | opc [16:15] = DEST type | 10000 [14:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0] (ARM ARM C7.2 FCVT). The width axis keys on the SOURCE (the MIR→LIR FPTrunc/FPExt arm threads a widthOverride from the source operand's type — the result-width default would select exactly the WRONG direction): F32 source → FCVT Dd, Sn (type=00, opc=01 → 0x1E22C000, the FPExt widen); F64 source → FCVT Sd, Dn (type=01, opc=00 → 0x1E624000, the FPTrunc narrow).

F32 source → FCVT Dd, Sn (widen to double).

opcodes.$comment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): FCVTZS Xd, Dn — double to signed 64-bit integer, round toward zero (FP→integer conversion). Base 0x9E780000 = sf=1 [31] | 00 | 11110 [28:24] | ftype=01 double [23:22] | 1 [21] | rmode=11 toward-zero [20:19] | opcode=000 FCVTZS [18:16] | 000000 [15:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0]. The result is GPR-class via the MIR integer type (regClassFor) — rd carries the X destination, the rn wire the D source; the 5-bit slots are class-blind hwEncodings, exactly the GPR-dest/FPR-src split x86's cvttsd2si makes through modrm.reg/modrm.rm. MIR FPToSI is the producer. FC3.5 sweep-c2: the F32-source sibling FCVTZS Xd, Sn (ftype=00 → 0x9E380000) rides the SOURCE-width axis (the FPToSI arm threads the source's width — the X destination is unchanged).

variants.$comment: FC3.5: FCVTZS Xd, Sn — ftype=00 single source, base 0x9E380000.

opcodes.$comment: c92 (D-CSUBSET-FP-TO-UI-CODEGEN, the c78 arm64 residual): FCVTZU — float to UNSIGNED integer, round toward zero. The EXACT MIRROR of fp_to_si above: same 'Conversion between FP and integer' group, same field layout (sf [31] | 00 | 11110 [28:24] | ftype [23:22] | 1 [21] | rmode=11 toward-zero [20:19] | opcode [18:16] | 000000 [15:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0]), opcode=001 FCVTZU where FCVTZS is 000 (+0x00010000). Same SOURCE-float-width axis (the mir_to_lir FPToUI arm threads the source's width, c78) and the same FIXED X destination as fp_to_si — a U32 result reads the low 32 bits of the Xd result, VALUE-CORRECT for any double/float in [0, 2^32) (the arm64 analog of x86 fp_to_ui's CVTTSD2SI r64 low-32 convention; gcc's `fcvtzu w0, d0` agrees on every in-range value, out-of-range is C 6.3.1.4p1 UB). ★ UNLIKE x86 (whose signed CVTTSD2SI needs the deferred >2^63 conditional-subtract, D-CSUBSET-UI-FROM-FP-UNSIGNED-I64), FCVTZU Xd covers the FULL unsigned-i64 range NATIVELY — that anchor is x86-ONLY; the arm64 leg has NO >2^63 residual (gcc emits the identical `fcvtzu x0, d0`). MIR FPToUI is the producer. FCVTZU Xd,Dn = 0x9E790000 = FCVTZS Xd,Dn[0x9E780000] | opcode bit [0x00010000]; FCVTZU Xd,Sn = 0x9E390000 = FCVTZS Xd,Sn[0x9E380000] | 0x00010000 (both cross-checked against the ARM ARM field decode above + aarch64-gcc objdump).

lowering.$comment: D-TARGET-ENCODING-TABLE-EXPRESSES-ONLY-THE-DEGENERATE-SEQUENCE. ★ THIS IS NOT A SPECIAL CASE AND NOT A `native` FLAG — it is the same kind of row x86-64's seven-step fp_to_ui carries, ONE ENTRY LONG, because on this machine the operation genuinely IS one instruction. Declaring it makes the statement uniform: every target STATES how the operation is realized, and the shared substrate reads one thing and emits what it was told. ✔MEASURED under qemu-aarch64 on all ten conversion probes (both directions, both source float widths, u32 and u64, at and above 2^31/2^63): 10/10 agree with gcc-13 and clang-19 — FCVTZU Xd is genuinely full-range from BOTH a Dn and an Sn source, so the one-step declaration is TRUE and not a half-truth. The step names this very opcode; that is well-founded, not circular, because a step is emitted as a MACHINE instruction and never re-expanded (the loader enforces it by requiring every step's opcode to declare an encoding).

variants.$comment: F64 source → FCVTZU Xd, Dn — ftype=01 double, base 0x9E790000 (the low 32 bits are the in-range U32 result; the full Xd is the NATIVE full-range U64).
F32 source → FCVTZU Xd, Sn — ftype=00 single, base 0x9E390000.

opcodes.$comment: D-CSUBSET-INT-FLOAT-CONVERSION (int→float): SCVTF — Scalar Convert Signed integer to Floating-point. The REVERSE of FCVTZS above. 'Conversion between FP and integer' group: sf [31] | 00 [30:29] | 11110 [28:24] | ftype [23:22] | 1 [21] | rmode=00 [20:19] | opcode=010 SCVTF [18:16] | 000000 [15:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0]. The result is FPR-class (regClassFor sees the F64 MIR result) — rd carries the D destination, the rn wire the X/W integer source; the 5-bit slots are class-blind hwEncodings, exactly the GPR-src/FPR-dest split x86's cvtsi2sd makes through modrm.rm/modrm.reg. MIR SIToFP is the producer. The width axis keys on the SOURCE INTEGER width (the mir_to_lir SIToFP arm threads the source's int width): a 64-bit source -> SCVTF Dd, Xn (sf=1, width=64), a 32-bit source -> SCVTF Dd, Wn (sf=0, width=32). UNLIKE x86's single REX.W bit, arm64 sf+ftype are INDEPENDENT, so BOTH source-int widths keep ftype=01 (the F64 DESTINATION, Dd) — `Dd,Wn` is the i32->f64 form, the arm64 analog of cvtsi2sd xmm,r32. DESIGN NOTE (audit + qemu-arm64 scrutiny — verify these fixedWords on real hardware): dest fixed at F64/Dd this cycle (the dominant + sqlite-blocking i64->double case); int->F32 (ftype=00, Sd) is FAIL-LOUD at the mir_to_lir SIToFP arm (a deferred narrow gap, D-CSUBSET-INT-TO-F32-CODEGEN). SCVTF Dd,Xn = 0x9E620000 = sf=1[0x80000000] | 11110[0x1E000000] | ftype=01[0x00400000] | bit21[0x00200000] | opcode=010[0x00020000]; SCVTF Dd,Wn = 0x1E620000 (same MINUS the sf bit). Cross-checked against the config's FCVTZS Dn base 0x9E780000 (opcode=000, rmode=11) — same field decode.

variants.$comment: SCVTF Dd, Xn — sf=1 64-bit signed source -> double. base 0x9E620000. The sqlite i64 -> volatile double blocker.
SCVTF Dd, Wn — sf=0 32-bit signed source -> double. base 0x1E620000 (the arm64 analog of cvtsi2sd xmm,r32; an I32 fits the F64 result exactly).

opcodes.$comment: D-CSUBSET-INT-FLOAT-CONVERSION (int→float, unsigned): UCVTF — Scalar Convert Unsigned integer to Floating-point. Same 'Conversion between FP and integer' group as SCVTF but opcode=011 [18:16] (the unsigned sibling). MIR UIToFP is the producer; the SOURCE-int-width axis matches si_to_fp (width=64 -> UCVTF Dd,Xn, width=32 -> UCVTF Dd,Wn). Dest fixed F64/Dd (U->F32 deferred D-CSUBSET-INT-TO-F32-CODEGEN). Unlike x86 SSE2 (which has no unsigned cvt and must fall back to cvtsi2sd), arm64 UCVTF handles the FULL unsigned i64 range natively — so the arm64 ui_to_fp is value-correct where x86's signed-cvt fallback is not (the deferred D-CSUBSET-UI-TO-FP-UNSIGNED-I64 is an x86-only gap; sqlite does not hit it on either target). UCVTF Dd,Xn = 0x9E630000 = SCVTF Dd,Xn[0x9E620000] | opcode bit [0x00010000]; UCVTF Dd,Wn = 0x1E630000.

lowering.$comment: D-TARGET-ENCODING-TABLE-EXPRESSES-ONLY-THE-DEGENERATE-SEQUENCE — the one-entry form of the same row x86-64 needs seven steps for. UCVTF Dd,Xn is full-range over the whole u64 and UCVTF Dd,Wn over the whole u32, so BOTH declarations are true at their declared width; the destination stays fixed at F64/Dd on this target, and an F32 destination still has no realization at all and fails loud upstream (D-CSUBSET-INT-TO-F32-CODEGEN) rather than being half-declared here.

UCVTF Dd, Wn — sf=0 32-bit unsigned source -> double. base 0x1E630000.

opcodes.$comment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): FMOV Dd, Dn — FP register-register move, double. Base 0x1E604000 = 0 0 0 11110 [31:24] | ftype=01 [23:22] | 1 [21] | opc=000000 FMOV [20:15] | 10000 [14:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0] (FP data-processing 1 source — the single source rides Rn, NOT Rm; contrast the GPR mov's ORR alias whose source is Rm). Bound to the fpr class's `move` slot in registerClassOps[] — consumed by MIR value/phi copies and the callconv arg/return moves whenever the register class is FPR (the arm64 analog of x86's movaps role; a D-form copy moves the full 64-bit view, no upper-lane-merge hazard to dodge). FC3.5 sweep-c2 adjudication: register COPIES stay width-BLIND (variant deliberately width-absent, match-any) — the D-form move preserves an F32 value exactly (it lives in the low 4 bytes; S[n] is the low half of D[n]), the same reasoning as x86's full-register MOVAPS serving both widths. Only memory accesses (fldur/fstur) are width-exact.

D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): FPR memory LOAD — LDUR Dt, [Xn, #simm9] (SIMD&FP 64-bit, unscaled). Fixed word 0xFC400000 = the GPR LDUR 0xF8400000 with V=1 (bit 26): size=11 [31:30] | 111 [29:27] | V=1 [26] | 00 [25:24] | opc=01 load [23:22] | 0 [21] | imm9 [20:12] | 00 [11:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rt [4:0]. Operand layout mirrors the GPR `load` row exactly (shared LIR load form [base_reg, MemBase(scale=1), MemOffset(disp)] + result): result→Rt (rd), base→Rn, MemOffset→Imm9 (signed -256..255), MemBase carries no bits (membase.noscale). Bound to the fpr class's `load` slot in registerClassOps[] — the callconv epilogue saved-d-reg reload, stack-resident F64 args, and MIR Load of an F64 rodata global (the literal-materialization path) all resolve here. F64-only: the F32 S-form (size=10, 0xBC400000) lands with an F32 consumer.

encoding.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c2 (D-CSUBSET-F32-CODEGEN): width-keyed pair — LDUR Dt (8-byte, 0xFC400000, width 64) vs LDUR St (4-byte, size=10 → 0xBC400000, width 32; ARM ARM C7.2 LDUR SIMD&FP). lowerLoad threads the loaded type's width for FPR-class results: an 8-byte D-load of a 4-byte F32 rodata item would read past the item.

variants.$comment: FC3.5: LDUR St, [Xn, #simm9] — size=10 single, base 0xBC400000 (4-byte load).

opcodes.$comment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): FPR memory STORE — STUR Dt, [Xn, #simm9] (SIMD&FP 64-bit, unscaled). Fixed word 0xFC000000 = the GPR STUR 0xF8000000 with V=1 (bit 26); opc=00 store. Operand layout mirrors the GPR `store` row exactly (shared LIR store form [value_reg, base_reg, MemBase(scale=1), MemOffset(disp)], no result): value→Rt (rd wire), base→Rn, MemOffset→Imm9 (signed). Bound to the fpr class's `store` slot in registerClassOps[] — the callconv prologue saved-d-reg spill is the first consumer (AAPCS64 declares d8-d15 callee-saved + regalloc prefers callee-saved, so the FIRST FPR vreg in any function needs this store — the exact shape that surfaced x86's movsd_store on ms_x64).

encoding.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c2: width-keyed pair — STUR Dt (8-byte, width 64) vs STUR St (4-byte, 0xBC000000, width 32). lowerStore threads the stored VALUE's type width for FPR-class stores; the regalloc spill path stays width-default 64 over 8-byte slots (value-preserving for both float widths).

opcodes.$comment: FC12c (D-FC12C-AAPCS64-VARIADIC-CALLEE, BLOCKER-1): FPR 128-bit memory STORE — STUR Qt, [Xn, #simm9] (SIMD&FP 128-bit, unscaled). Used to spill the v0..v7 VR arg registers (16-byte slots) into the AAPCS64 variadic register-save-area's VR block so va_arg(double) reads the right 8 bytes. CRITICAL fixedWord = 0x3C800000 = 1015021568, NOT 0x3C000000: the latter is STURB (8-bit byte store) and would spill one byte per FP slot → va_arg(double) garbage. Derivation (ARM ARM C7 LDR/STR SIMD&FP unscaled, 128-bit): Q form size[31:30]=00, [29:27]=111, V[26]=1, opc[23:22]=10 (store, 128-bit) → 0x00000000(size=00) | 0x38000000([29:27]=111) | 0x04000000(V=1,[26]) | 0x00800000(opc=10,[23:22]) = 0x3C800000. Operand layout is IDENTICAL to the D/S-form fstur rows above (shared LIR store form [value_reg, base_reg, MemBase(scale=1), MemOffset(disp)], no result): value→Rt (rd wire), base→Rn, MemOffset→Imm9 (signed -256..255). Single 128-bit form (no width variants — Q is always 16 bytes). Byte-pin: STUR Q0,[X1,#0] = 0x3C800000 (Rd=0,Rn=1<<5=0x20,Imm9=0 → 0x3C800020), LE bytes 20 00 80 3C.

D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-IEEE128-ARITH (LD-2): FPR 128-bit memory LOAD — LDUR Qt, [Xn, #simm9] (SIMD&FP 128-bit, unscaled). The load sibling of fstur_q above: same size=00/[29:27]=111/V=1 encoding with opc=11 (128-bit LOAD) instead of 10 (store). CRITICAL fixedWord = 0x3CC00000 = 1019215872: fstur_q's 0x3C800000 with opc bit [23]=1 (opc 10→11). Derivation (ARM ARM C7 LDR/STR SIMD&FP unscaled, 128-bit): size[31:30]=00, [29:27]=111 (0x38000000), V[26]=1 (0x04000000), opc[23:22]=11 load-128 (0x00C00000) → 0x3CC00000. Operand layout mirrors the D/S-form fldur row exactly (shared LIR load form [base_reg, MemBase(scale=1), MemOffset(disp)] + result): result→Rt (rd), base→Rn, MemOffset→Imm9 (signed -256..255), MemBase carries no bits. Single 128-bit form (no width variants — Q is always 16 bytes). Byte-pin: LDUR Q0,[X1,#0] = 0x3CC00000 (Rd=0, Rn=1<<5=0x20, Imm9=0 → 0x3CC00020), LE bytes 20 00 C0 3C. Bound to the vr class's `load` slot in registerClassOps[] — the F128 softcall verb's operand marshalling (fldur_q vN <- [home]) is its sole consumer.

$condCodeEncodingComment: D-AS3-COND-CODE-ARM64 (mirror of x86's table): per-cond-code nibble for the AArch64 B.cond instruction's bits [3:0]. Numeric values are the AArch64 condition codes (ARM ARM C1.2.4): EQ=0, NE=1, CS/HS=2, CC/LO=3, HI=8, LS=9, GE=10(0xA), LT=11(0xB), GT=12(0xC), LE=13(0xD). Signed comparisons map slt→LT(0xB)=11, sle→LE(0xD)=13, sgt→GT(0xC)=12, sge→GE(0xA)=10; unsigned map ult→CC/LO=3, ule→LS=9, ugt→HI=8, uge→CS/HS=2. The encoder ORs this nibble into word 0 bits 0..3 of the jcc macro (vs x86's low 4 bits of the opcode byte — same field-position abstraction, different ISA placement). The 10 integer arms are REQUIRED; the FC3.5 float arms (next comment) are per-entry optional.
$condCodeEncodingFloatComment: FC3.5 sweep-c2 (FCmp lowering — D-COND-FLOAT-NAN-TRUTHINESS-FCMP): float condition arms over the FCMP NZCV truth table (ARM ARM: equal → Z=1,C=1; less → N=1; greater → C=1; unordered → C=1,V=1). fogt = GT (Z=0∧N=V, 0xC — unordered has N=0≠V=1 → false ✓; NOTE the integer-ugt HI=8 would be TRUE on unordered, a NaN miscompile — this is why float codes are separate); foge = GE (N=V, 0xA); foeq = EQ (Z=1, 0 — unordered Z=0 → false ✓); fune = NE (Z=0, 1 — TRUE on unordered, exactly C 6.5.9 `!=`); fuo = VS (V=1, 6 — after FCMP the overflow flag IS the unordered predicate); ford = VC (7). fone is deliberately ABSENT: NE is true on unordered, and no single AArch64 cond is `ordered ∧ unequal` — its absence signals the composed realization (One = cset-NE ∧ cset-VC), the mirror of x86's foeq/fune absence. Olt/Ole need no entries — the lowering swap-canonicalizes them to fogt/foge (MI/LS would also realize them directly; the swap keeps ONE target-blind rule).
$registersComment: AAPCS64 general-purpose registers x0..x30 + zero-register XZR (encoded as 31 in source operands; uses register's hwEncoding). Stack pointer `sp` is also encoded as 31 but in the SP-slot context — hwEncoding=31 with class GPR is shared between XZR and SP at the byte level. D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): the SIMD&FP file is declared as d0..d31 (class fpr) — the V registers' 64-bit D views, sharing the same 5-bit field encoding.

registers.$comment: Stack pointer shares hwEncoding=31 with XZR at the byte level (the context determines which: SP-using addressing modes vs ZR-encoding instructions). The substrate treats them as distinct names with distinct ordinals; the JSON-side ordinal is what matters for the cc lookup.
registers.name: sp

registers.$comment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): the V-register file's 64-bit D views, class fpr. FC3.5 sweep-c2: F32 values live in the S views (the low 32 bits of the same registers) — the width axis on the instruction VARIANTS selects D vs S forms; the register declarations stay the D views (the 5-bit hwEncoding is shared by every view, and copies/spills move the containing D view, value-preserving for F32). widthBytes=8 is the D view, NOT the full 128-bit V register — the q/v views (and their subOf aliasing) are the future F128/SIMD cycle's work. hwEncoding = the 5-bit register number every SIMD&FP instruction form shares.
registers.name: d0

registers.$comment: D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-IEEE128-ARITH (LD-2): the V-register file's FULL 128-bit Q views, class vr. widthBytes=16 (the whole SIMD&FP register, NOT the d/s sub-views above). The 5-bit hwEncoding is SHARED with the matching d-view (v0/d0 both encode register number 0) — the fldur_q/fstur_q Q-form memory ops the registerClassOps `vr` row binds address these by that shared encoding. These rows are DELIBERATELY absent from the AAPCS64 calling-convention register lists (argFprs/callerSaved/calleeSaved name the d-views), so lir_regalloc's buildFreeLists SKIPS them (not allocatable) — no VR virtual register is ever minted; the F128 softcall verb uses v0/v1 as PHYSICAL transient scratch around the BL, and the BL's caller-saved clobber of the aliased d0-d7 is what keeps a live double off them (the x87 st0/st1 precedent, one axis over). A future SIMD/vector cycle that makes VR allocatable must add the subOf aliasing + callerSaved membership then (the calleeSaved d8-d15 caveat in $calleeSavedFprComment applies).
registers.name: v0

registers.$comment: ★★ THE 32-BIT W VIEWS — the arm64 half of `subOf`'s first real consumer (2026-08-13); see the x86_64 twin for the full rationale. `w0` is the low 32 bits of `x0`: ONE machine register, two spellings, and the ISA distinguishes them by the instruction's sf bit rather than by a register number (the 5-bit hwEncoding is shared). So a narrow spelling resolves to the parent ordinal and the width rides the LIR instruction. `wzr` is included because it is the W view of `xzr` and `mov w0, wzr` is how AArch64 spells a 32-bit zero; `wsp` is omitted (no consumer). ⚠ NOT ALLOCATABLE, and the mechanism changed on 2026-08-13 — this sentence used to say 'both allocator paths skip a non-empty `subOf`'. BOTH skips have been DELETED as unreachable defence: ✔MEASURED, `allocatable` is built EXCLUSIVELY from the six calling-convention lists, so a row named in none of them could never enter a pool for a skip to catch. A calling convention naming a `subOf` register is now REFUSED AT CONFIG LOAD (`TargetSchemaData::validate()`'s `checkRefs`, `C_MalformedJson` with the offending JSON path). These rows appear in no cc list, which is now enforced rather than merely true.
registers.name: w0

$asmConstraintsComment:
★★★ WHICH GNU INLINE-ASM CONSTRAINT LETTER MEANS WHICH REGISTER IS TARGET VOCABULARY — see the twin block in x86_64.target.json for the full rationale and for the [[D-CONFIG-ASM-DIALECT-DECLARED-AS-TARGET-VOCABULARY]] line this facet is drawn on. What THIS file adds is the proof that the mapping is config and not code.
★★ THIS TARGET IS THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE THAT MAKES THE FACET NECESSARY. ✔MEASURED, aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 `-O2 -S`: `"=a"` here is `error: impossible constraint in 'asm'` — and so are `b`, `c`, `d`, `D` and `q`, every one of which x86_64 declares. A shared C++ table would have had to branch on the architecture to say that; this file says it by SAYING NOTHING, and the consumer's refusal renders the valid list from whichever target it was handed.
✔MEASURED, aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 `-O2 -S`, with three competing live `"r"` operands: r→x0, w→v0, `"m"(*p)`→`[x0]`, `"i"(7)`→`7`. ⚠ THE COMPILER IS NAMED HERE BECAUSE ITS ABSENCE COST A CYCLE. Every arrow in this block is what **gcc PRINTS** — the evidence that the binding on the row below is the right one. It is not, and never was, a claim about what THIS compiler emits. An elided subject read as one: a lane took `"m"(*p)`→`[x0]` for a DSS capability claim, found the pipeline refusing the letter, and filed the two halves as a contradiction inside one config (D-ASM-MEMORY-CONSTRAINT-REFUSED-DESPITE-BEING-DECLARED). The row was RIGHT and the pipeline was WRONG — `"m"` is realized end-to-end now, witnessed by execution in `examples/c/c_inline_asm_memory_operand`. ⇒ the subject of a measurement is STATED in this file, never inferred from the paragraph it sits in. ⚠ NOTE `i` → `7` with NO sigil while x86_64 emits `$7`: the sigil is DIALECT grammar, which is exactly why the operandKind (`imm32`) is identical on both targets and the printing is not this file's business.
★ `w` → `vr`, NOT `fpr`, AND THE MEASUREMENT SETTLES IT RATHER THAN INTUITION. gcc's `w` is the V register file; the natural guess is that a `double` bound with `"=w"` should be `d0`. ✔MEASURED: `double dw(double a){ __asm__("# W %0 %1" : "=w"(o) : "w"(a)); }` emits `# W v0 v0` — gcc's DEFAULT print for a `w` operand is the V-register name regardless of the C type. The `d0`/`s0` narrow spellings come from the `%d0`/`%s0` operand MODIFIERS, which are dialect grammar and live with the dialect. So `vr` is the exact answer and `fpr` would have been the plausible wrong one.
⚠ DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED: `x` and `y`. Both bind V registers here (✔MEASURED x→v0, y→v0), and the restriction is MEASURED, not taken from the letter's documented meaning — the probe pushes N simultaneous live operands through one asm and reads the largest N that still compiles: **r=30, w=30, x=16, y=8**. ★ READ THOSE CAREFULLY: 30 is the ALLOCATOR CEILING, not a set size — `r` and `w` both stop there, and this target declares 65 gpr / 32 vr rows — so `w` is only proven to be ≥30 and is taken as the full V file. `x`=16 and `y`=8 sit BELOW that ceiling, which is what makes them genuine subclass measurements (V0-V15 and V0-V7) rather than 'too many operands'. The `w` control clinches it: it COMPILES the identical 18-operand asm that `x` refuses, printing `v0 v1 v2 v3 v4 v5 v6 v7 v16 v17 v18 v19 v20 v21 v22 v23 v24 v25`. TargetRegClass cannot express a SUBSET, so declaring `x` or `y` as plain `vr` would load clean, read as support, and hand the allocator registers gcc forbids ⇒ the same refusal x86_64 applies to `Q`, and the deferral is stated in full in that file's twin comment (a FOURTH binding axis — an explicit register-name list — deliberately not built; trigger: the first client whose inline asm uses a subclass letter, which ✔MEASURED none does today).
⚠ Also absent: `k` (the stack pointer). ✔MEASURED in BOTH directions — `"=k"` as an output AND `"k"` as an input are each `error: inconsistent operand constraints in an 'asm'` — so there is no measured binding to declare. The two-direction check matters: an earlier note asserted only the output half, which would have left the input half an untested guess sitting inside a sentence that read as a measurement.

asmConstraints.$comment: The general-register class. ✔x0 — and x86_64's SAME letter `r` resolves into a register set that contains rax and no x0. One letter, two targets, disjoint registers: the operator-required proof that this mapping is config, not code.

✔MEASURED `"m"(*p)` → `[x0]` — a DIFFERENT printed form from x86_64's `(%rdi)` for the identical `membase` binding, which is the vocabulary/grammar split visible in one line. ★ REALIZED END-TO-END, AND THAT SENTENCE IS NEW: the pipeline used to REFUSE this letter with `has no resolved register class — the constraint letter was never bound to a processor`, about the row you are reading. The resolution carried only two of `binds`’ three arms, so a declared form-bound letter was byte-identical to an undeclared one. The ADDRESS is what gets a register; the form decides what the template writes around it. (D-ASM-MEMORY-CONSTRAINT-REFUSED-DESPITE-BEING-DECLARED; witnessed by execution in `examples/c/c_inline_asm_memory_operand`.) ★ THE OUTPUT DIRECTION (`"=m"`, `"+m"`, `"=&m"`) IS REALIZED TOO, BY THE SAME CARRIAGE: the operand's ADDRESS in a register, with the direction living entirely inside the template's own instruction (D-ASM-MEMORY-CONSTRAINT-OUTPUT-FORM-NOT-REALIZED; witnessed by execution in `examples/c/c_inline_asm_memory_output_operand`, whose aarch64 arms run under qemu). ⚠ THIS SENTENCE REPLACED ONE THAT SAID THE OPPOSITE and had gone stale one cycle after it was written (*"a different mechanism and is still refused BY NAME"*); a config comment that reads as evidence is worth exactly as much as its last re-measurement (D-CONFIG-ASM-CONSTRAINT-COMMENT-CLAIMS-A-REFUSAL-THAT-NO-LONGER-EXISTS).

✔MEASURED, aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 `-O2 -S`: `"i"(7)` → a bare `7`, where x86_64 prints `$7` for the IDENTICAL `imm32` binding — the sigil is DIALECT grammar, which is why the operandKind is the same on both targets and the printing is not this file's business. ★ REALIZED END-TO-END, AND THAT SENTENCE IS NEW: the pipeline used to REFUSE this letter by name (`binds the operand form 'imm32', which this pipeline does not yet realize`) while this row correctly declared it. An immediate binds NO register — the number is written INTO the instruction — so the VALUE travels instead, as an ordinary MIR `Const`. (D-ASM-IMMEDIATE-CONSTRAINT-FORM-NOT-REALIZED; witnessed by execution in `examples/c/c_inline_asm_immediate_operand`, which emits `add x28, x28, #0x5` here and `add $0x5,%r14d` on x86_64.) ⚠ THE OPERAND MUST BE AN INTEGER CONSTANT EXPRESSION AND IS PROVEN ONE, NOT ASSUMED: ✔MEASURED, gcc 13.3.0 at -O0 AND -O2 on THIS target, a runtime value here is `error: impossible constraint in 'asm'`, and DSS refuses it too. The accepted set is gcc's — `"i"(1+2)` → `3`, `"i"(sizeof(int))` → `4`. An `"=i"` OUTPUT is refused on both sides (gcc: `output number 0 not directly addressable`). ⓘ THE TARGET'S OWN ENCODING GUARDS STILL APPLY UNDERNEATH: `add`'s imm12 variant declares `immMax: 4095` and a larger value falls through to the shifted word-pair — the constraint says the operand is a 32-bit immediate, the opcode rows say how each value is spelled in bytes.

$registerClassOpsComment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): per-register-class move/load/store mnemonics — the same FC2 Part B table x86_64 declares. A class WITHOUT a row uses the universal defaults (mov/load/store) iff it is gpr — the substrate default class; every other row-less class FAILS LOUD at the consumer (L_RequiredLirOpcodeMissing), because the class-blind alternative is a silent miscompile (a GPR ORR/LDUR against a D-register hwEncoding assembles to valid-looking words that move the WRONG register file). fpr: move=FMOV(D), load=LDUR(D), store=STUR(D).

registerClassOps.$comment: D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-IEEE128-ARITH (LD-2): the 128-bit VR (Q-view) class carries only load=fldur_q / store=fstur_q — the F128 softcall verb LOADS an operand's 16-byte memory home into a physical arg Q-register (v0/v1) and STORES the result Q-register back to a fresh home. NO `move` (trigger discipline): the softcall never register-copies a full Q value class-internally (the value is memory-resident; only its 16 bytes move through fldur_q/fstur_q), so declaring a Q-form FMOV with no consumer would be dead vocabulary. An omitted slot fails loud at the consumer, exactly like the fpr row's discipline.

$wideFloatSoftcallsComment: D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-IEEE128-ARITH (LD-2): the softfloat runtime-libcall table for IEEE binary128 `long double` arithmetic. Each row names the libgcc helper an F128 op lowers to a CALL of, plus the physical registers the operands/result are marshalled through (AAPCS64: __*tf3 take two Q-register quad args in v0/v1 and return the quad in v0; __fixtfsi takes the quad in v0 and returns the int32 in x0; __extenddftf2 takes a double in d0 and returns the quad in v0). The MIR→LIR engine keys the softcall verb on TypeKind::F128 + the PRESENCE of the row for the op (wideFloatSoftcall(op) != nullptr) — NEVER a target-name/format check; a target that declares F128 but omits this table falls straight through to the requireEncodedFloatWidth fail-loud gate (the load-bearing agnosticism condition). The helper symbols live in libgcc_s.so.1 (see wideFloatSoftcallLibraryByFormat); the lowerer auto-injects the extern import on first use.
$wideFloatSoftcallLibraryComment: D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-IEEE128-ARITH (LD-2): the DT_NEEDED library each minted softcall extern binds to, keyed by object-format name. The aarch64 softfloat helpers (__addtf3 family) live in libgcc_s.so.1 (verified present in /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu/lib/libgcc_s.so.1), versioned @@GCC_3.0 — a single default version, so the extern import is UNVERSIONED (binds the default, as the setjmp imports do). Only `elf` is declared: the f64-axis formats (pe64/macho-arm64) collapse long double to double and never reach the softcall path; the x87-80 axis (elf/macho x86_64) uses the inline x87 sequence (LD-1), not a libcall.
$callingConventionsComment: AAPCS64 (https://github.com/ARM-software/abi-aa/blob/main/aapcs64/aapcs64.rst). Integer args: x0..x7. FP args: d0..d7 (D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE 2026-06-10 — declared with the FPR substrate). Caller-saved: x0..x18 (incl. x16/x17 = IP0/IP1; PLT-clobberable) + v0-v7/v16-v31 in their d views. Callee-saved: x19..x28 + x29 (frame ptr) + x30 (link reg) + v8-v15 low 64 bits (d8..d15).

callingConventions.name: aapcs64
callingConventions.$argVrsComment: D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-AGGREGATE-ABI (LD-4): AAPCS64 §5.4 — an IEEE binary128 `long double` (or a binary128 HFA piece) is passed in a full 128-bit SIMD&FP register v0..v7 and returned in v0..v3. These are the Q-VIEW (vr class) names of the SAME registers the d-view argFprs/returnFprs list, so an F128 arg at NSRN k lands in v{k} which aliases d{k} = argFprs[k] — an F64 and an F128 sharing a signature never collide by ordinal (the shared NGRN/NSRN counter). The MIR→LIR F128 boundary verb reads these lists (name->ordinal, like argFprs) to marshal an F128 arg into v{k} (fldur_q) and capture the v0 return (fstur_q). Parallel to argFprs; NOT a new register-allocation pool (the vr rows are non-allocatable transient scratch — the v0/d0-aliasing safety net from LD-2 applies).
callingConventions.$aggregateComment: FC7 C3 (D-FC7-STRUCT-BY-VALUE-ARG-RETURN): AAPCS64 §5.4 by-value aggregates. HFA (1-4 leaves all the same FP type) → that many FPR pieces (v0..v3 / d0..d3 for returns, d0..d7 for args). A non-HFA aggregate <=16 bytes → 1-2 GPR pieces (x0..x1 returns / x0..x7 args); > 16 bytes → BY REFERENCE: a caller-allocated copy for args; for RETURNS the caller passes the result address in x8 (`indirectResultRegister`) and the callee returns VOID (it writes through x8 — distinct from SysV/Win64's hidden-arg-then-return-pointer; `aggregateSretViaHiddenArg` is false here because indirectResultRegister is set). `aapcs64_hfa` drives the bounded classifier arm; maxRegBytes = 16 (two X-registers).
callingConventions.$aggregateStackExhaustsComment: D-FC12-VARIADIC-OVERFLOW-FIXED-AGGREGATE-STACK-ARGS: AAPCS64 §6.4.2 stage C — when a by-value composite/HFA does not fit the remaining arg registers it is placed WHOLLY on the stack and the overflowed class is EXHAUSTED (gcc aarch64_layout_arg sets aapcs_nextncrn=8 / aapcs_nextnvrn=8), so every subsequent arg of that class also goes to memory. true = no backfill (contrast SysV, which backfills the leftover registers). Read by HIR→MIR's caller+callee cursor handling + va_start's __gr_offs/__vr_offs clamp.
callingConventions.$callerSavedFprComment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): AAPCS64 §6.1.2 — v0-v7 (args/results) and v16-v31 are caller-saved; declared here in their d views. Being listed in callerSaved is what keeps the regalloc honest about them: an allocatable register NOT in callerSaved is treated as call-safe (lir_regalloc buildFreeLists), so omitting these while argFprs makes them allocatable would let a float live across a call sit unsaved in a volatile d-register — the same reason x86_64's sysv row lists all sixteen xmm registers here.
callingConventions.$calleeSavedFprComment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): AAPCS64 §6.1.2 — v8-v15 must be preserved by a callee ONLY in their LOW 64 BITS; the top 64 bits are caller's responsibility everywhere. The d8..d15 rows are therefore EXACTLY the preserved contract for F64 (the prologue's D-form STUR saves precisely the bits the ABI guarantees — the same low-64-only shape as Win64's xmm6-15/MOVSD). CAVEAT for a future F128/SIMD cycle: a Q/V-register value live across a call must NOT rely on these rows — the callee preserves only the low half; re-examine when q/v views land.
callingConventions.$framePointerComment: D-CSUBSET-VLA (C1b): x29 is the AAPCS64 frame-pointer register a VLA function reserves as a stable fixed-frame base (captured at the fixed-frame bottom via `sp_copy`, then every fixed-frame ref switches SP->x29 so it survives the runtime `sub sp,<vlaSize>`). A NON-VLA function never reserves it — x29 stays an ordinary callee-saved allocatable GPR (byte-identical frames). Consumed by lir_regalloc (pool exclusion) + lir_callconv (force-save + prologue capture + epilogue restore).
callingConventions.$entryStackPointerBiasComment: D-LK10-ENTRY-TRAMP-PROLOGUE: AArch64 BL does NOT push a return address (it writes LR / x30 directly), so process entry — whether by kernel-jump (Linux/Mac) or `RtlUserThreadStart`-BL (Windows) — leaves SP 16-byte-aligned (bias 0 mod 16). Trampoline `sub sp, 0` is emitted as nothing — `alignedSizeWithBias(shadowSpaceBytes=0, stackAlignment=16, bias=0) = 0`.
callingConventions.$callPushBytesComment: D-LK10-ENTRY-ML7-FRAME-BIAS-UNIFY: AArch64 BL writes the return address into LR/x30 — no stack push. callPushBytes=0 is the right ISA-level fact for ARM64. Non-leaf functions on ARM64 still save x30 in their prologue + reload it before `ret`; because x30 is the `linkRegister` (deliberately NOT in `calleeSaved` — it must not be allocatable), this is realized by the link-register fold in `lir_callconv.cpp::materializeOneFunc` (gated on hasCalls + cc.linkRegister), which adds x30 to `savedRegs` so it lands in `savedRegAreaSize`. Without it the epilogue `ret` returns to a clobbered LR — see D-LK10-ENTRY-ARM64-NONLEAF-LINK-REGISTER. Independent of the call-push bias.
callingConventions.$vaListLayoutComment: FC12c (D-FC12C-AAPCS64-VARIADIC-CALLEE): AAPCS64 §B.4 dual-cursor variadic callee. `__va_list` = {void* __stack@0; void* __gr_top@8; void* __vr_top@16; int __gr_offs@24; int __vr_offs@28;} (32B). The prologue spills x0..x7 (GR block, 8×8=64B) then v0..v7 (VR block, 8×16=128B) into a callee-local register-save-area (regSaveAreaBytes()=192). va_start sets __gr_top=rsa+64 (past the GR block), __vr_top=rsa+192 (past the VR block), __stack=overflow base, __gr_offs=-(8-fixedGpr)*8, __vr_offs=-(8-fixedFpr)*16. va_arg(T) classifies T (GPR vs VR), reads the negative class cursor, and if <0 reads `<gr|vr>_top + (sign-extended cursor)` then bumps by the slot stride, else walks __stack by 8 (the NSAA round-up quantum, even for a double). namedArgSlotBytes=8.

callingConventions.$comment: apple_arm64 — Apple's ARM64 ABI for Apple platforms (developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms). The ABI catalog (abi_catalog.cpp) maps (arm64, MachO) → CcApple → "apple_arm64"; shipping this row CLOSES D-FF3-5 (trigger: 'apple_arm64 cc row ships in arm64.target.json') and is what lets `resolveAbi` + the entry trampoline resolve a Mach-O-ARM64 cc. The general-purpose REGISTER vocabulary is IDENTICAL to AAPCS64 — integer args x0..x7, returns x0/x1, callee-saved x19..x28+x29, link x30, sp, 16-byte stack alignment, bias 0 (BL writes LR, no push). The Apple ABI's documented DIVERGENCES from AAPCS64 are NOT register-assignment differences: (1) variadic args are ALWAYS passed on the stack (vs AAPCS64's register-then-stack) and (2) a different indirect-result-location rule. Neither is modeled at today's scalar-only asm tier (variadic support is gated at D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-VARIADIC-SIGNATURE), so for the scalar register-passing this row carries the same fields as aapcs64; a SEPARATE named row keeps the ABI identity explicit and correct, so when variadic/indirect-result lands it is updated HERE, not by silently reusing aapcs64. The always-stack variadic rule + indirect-result-location divergence are pinned at D-FF3-APPLE-ARM64-ABI-DIVERGENCE (they land WITH the proper CcApple field set when the trigger fires — a variadic OR struct-return call on arm64-Apple — not as a silent aapcs64 reuse; distinct from D-FF3-4, which is the Microsoft CcMSARM64 split).
callingConventions.name: apple_arm64
callingConventions.$argVrsComment: D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-AGGREGATE-ABI (LD-4): carried for FIELD UNIFORMITY (so the `target.callingConvention(0)`-at-MIR->LIR convention stays valid regardless of which cc index is active) — but INERT on Apple: macho-arm64 is the f64 long-double axis, so `long double` IS `double` and no F128 TypeKind ever forms to reach the VR boundary verb. Apple's binary128 register-assignment matches AAPCS64 (the documented divergences are variadic/small-int, not FP-register placement), so the same v0..v7 / v0..v3 lists are correct if a future non-f64 arm64-Apple axis ever forms an F128.
callingConventions.$aggregateComment: FC7 C3: Apple ARM64 by-value aggregate register-assignment is IDENTICAL to AAPCS64 (the documented Apple divergences are variadic-always-stack + small-int widening, NOT the struct/HFA/x8 rules) — so it carries the same aggregate fields. This CLOSES the struct-return / indirect-result half of D-FF3-APPLE-ARM64-ABI-DIVERGENCE (x8 sret modeled); the variadic-always-stack half stays open until a variadic arm64-Apple call.
callingConventions.$aggregateStackExhaustsComment: D-FC12-VARIADIC-OVERFLOW-FIXED-AGGREGATE-STACK-ARGS: Apple arm64 inherits AAPCS64 stage-C register assignment (the Apple divergences are variadic-always-stack + small-int widening, NOT the composite placement rule) — a stacked composite EXHAUSTS the overflowed class, same as aapcs64.
callingConventions.$stackArgPackingComment: D-CODEGEN-APPLE-ARM64-STACK-ARGS-NOT-NATURALLY-PACKED — the NON-variadic half of D-FF3-APPLE-ARM64-ABI-DIVERGENCE, and the three axes MEASURED to differ rather than one boolean. Apple clang 21.0.0 / macOS 26.5.2, `otool -tV` of a `-target arm64-apple-macos` object, against `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0` `objdump -d` on the same sources (2026-08-24): (1) NAMED SCALARS pack NATURALLY — `char,short,int,long,char` land at +0,+2,+4,+8,+16 and `float,float,double,float` at +0,+4,+8,+16 (the FPR pool obeys the same rule), where AAPCS64 uses one 8-byte slot each (+0,+8,+16,+24); (2) NAMED AGGREGATES keep whole 8-byte slots on BOTH — a 3-byte struct then an `int` puts the int at +8, a 12-byte struct puts it at +16; (3) VARIADIC args keep 8-byte slots on BOTH — Apple's caller emits `str x` at +8,+16. A single boolean would therefore encode Apple's own ABI wrongly on two of the three axes. Omitting a key means "slot", so aapcs64/sysv/ms_x64 declare nothing and stay byte-identical.
callingConventions.$fprComment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): the SIMD&FP register vocabulary is IDENTICAL to AAPCS64 (Apple's documented divergences are variadic/indirect-result rules, not register assignment): args d0..d7, return d0, v0-v7/v16-v31 caller-saved, v8-v15 callee-saved in their LOW 64 BITS only (d8..d15 — same F128/SIMD-cycle caveat as the aapcs64 row's $calleeSavedFprComment).
callingConventions.$framePointerComment: D-CSUBSET-VLA (C1b): x29 is the AAPCS64 frame-pointer register a VLA function reserves as a stable fixed-frame base (captured at the fixed-frame bottom via `sp_copy`, then every fixed-frame ref switches SP->x29 so it survives the runtime `sub sp,<vlaSize>`). A NON-VLA function never reserves it — x29 stays an ordinary callee-saved allocatable GPR (byte-identical frames). Consumed by lir_regalloc (pool exclusion) + lir_callconv (force-save + prologue capture + epilogue restore).
callingConventions.$variadicComment: FC12c (D-FC12C-APPLE-ARM64-VARIADIC-CALLEE): the variadic half of D-FF3-APPLE-ARM64-ABI-DIVERGENCE. Apple arm64 passes ALL variadic args on the stack (vs AAPCS64's register-then-stack), so `va_list` is a PLAIN POINTER (HomogeneousPointer strategy, like Win64) that linearly bumps over the contiguous overflow area — no register-save-area, no dual cursor. `variadicArgsAlwaysStack` forces the CALLER to stack every vararg past the fixed args; `variadicUsesOverflowBase` makes va_start anchor `ap` at the overflow (first stacked vararg) base rather than a home area (Apple has none — named args stay in their registers, read via SSA). namedArgSlotBytes=8.

$relocationsComment: AArch64 ELF relocation kinds (plan 13 AS4 + plan 14 LK6 cycle 1 + D-LK6-1 closure 2026-06-01). The 'formula' field is a closed-enum discriminator (RelocFormulaKind in target_schema.hpp): 'aarch64_call26' = (S+A-P)>>2, signed-26-bit, OR into BL/B inst[25:0]; 'aarch64_adr_prel_pg_hi21' = ((S+A)>>12)-(P>>12), signed-21-bit, ADRP-split into immlo[30:29]+immhi[23:5]; 'aarch64_add_abs_lo12' = (S+A)&0xFFF, ADD imm12[21:10]; 'linear' (used for abs64) writes 8 LE bytes. Tag values are arbitrary per-target — only the NAME round-trips with format.json cross-reference. Paired anchors: D-LK6-8 (ARM64 PLT stub bytes) + D-LK6-14 (Apple Silicon chained-fixups dispatch) remain open and are independent of the formula reshape.

relocations.$comment: TLS C2 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): the local-exec thread-pointer-offset pair — the imm12 fields of the `lea` [reg, symbol] ADD/ADD macro. S = the SIGNED tpoff the walker bit-casts into symbolVa (arm64 Variant I ⇒ POSITIVE: alignUp(tcbHeaderBytes 16, p_align) + templateOffset). hi12 = (S+A)>>12 via the NEW Aarch64TprelAddHi12 formula — the pair's RANGE GATE ([0, 0xFFFFFF]; a silent wrap would address the wrong per-thread slot, audit LOW-d). lo12 = (S+A)&0xFFF — the SAME Aarch64AddAbsLo12 formula as add_abs_lo12_nc but a DISTINCT tls-flagged KIND row: the walker's CRIT-1 cross-check keys (target ∈ tlsSymbols) XOR (kind.tls) both directions, so reusing kind 3 for a tpoff patch would either reject loud (tls symbol under a non-tls kind) or — with the flag moved — mis-admit VA patches as tpoffs. `tls: true` is what marks the patched value a tpoff, not a VA.
